reason: With the declared general module-category, Gabriel-localization and adjoint infrastructure allowed, this is still an independent research-level image theorem for homological spectra of big tensor-triangulated categories. Its solution must establish the source-local weak-ring/maximal-localizing-ideal comparison, prove maximality of a pulled-back residue prime and lift an injective direct summand, then force existence of a prime above a point by a finitely-presented kernel witness and the projection formula. This is a structural result about noncompact support, not a routine auxiliary lemma or a long proof regraded by length. H3 is conditional on all these local arguments remaining solution obligations.
core_assessment: Independently read every selected statement, proof and context range before the selector rationale. The injective weak-ring construction uses flatness and injectivity to split the unit after tensoring and lifts that split through the pure-injective Hom identification. For a larger proper localizing ideal, the two-stage Gabriel quotient shows its unit injective hull equals the original one: an injective-hull summand becomes the entire hull after quotienting, and the residual summand is both local and killed, hence zero. This proves uniqueness of the maximal localizing ideal and converts internal-Hom support into a quotient test. A flat nonzero weak-ring unit is monic by finite-presented simplicity, giving the support equality used for U(1). In the residue pullback, the finite-generation theorem gives the kernel; simplicity forces maximality, and the induced exact quotient functor/right adjoint transports an injective hull so E_B splits off U(E_C). The forward image inclusion follows from the unital action of U(1) on U(E_C). For the reverse inclusion, assuming F(E_B)=0 makes F(I)=1 for I=ker(1->hat E_B). Since I is a filtered union of finitely presented subobjects and 1 is finitely presented, some M subset I has F(M)=1 (the map is also monic by exactness). M is in B, and the projection formula forces E_B tensor U(1)=0, contradicting the support assumption. Thus the annihilator ideal is proper and a maximal over-ideal pulls back to B.
prerequisite_assessment: The supplied ordinary category-theoretic infrastructure is explicitly named and its used statements are recalled in294-394 and423-443. The finite-presented generation result invoked at762 is also declared. None supplies the local comparison E_B=E_C, pulled-back prime maximality, injective-hull summand, or image theorem for free. The externally allowed homological nilpotence theorem appears only in the retained additional weak-ring zero-detection conclusion at705; the image equality does not need that extra conclusion. The generic existence of maximal Serre tensor ideals follows from the unit criterion and unions of chains, with no additional research input.
